paragraphs: In Lewisham, children who cannot live at home are cared for by the council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as those on this page. The council says it looks to its own carers first when it needs a home for a child, which makes it more likely that children can stay in the borough near their school and family.

Lewisham says it is urgently looking for carers who can look after children with complex and developmental needs. It also recruits for emergency, short-term and long-term fostering, teenagers (a two-adult household is needed), sibling groups of two to six children, teenage parents and their babies, parent and baby placements, and young people seeking asylum. You need to be 21 or over, with no upper age limit, and a spare bedroom for each child over five.

The council describes a typical payment of £350 to £500 a week per placement, rising to as much as £650 for a child with complex needs, depending on the child's age and the carer's experience. Nothing is paid between placements. Carers can recommend friends through a referral scheme that pays £500 when the new carer is approved and another £500 when a child is placed.

Support includes a supervising social worker, an out-of-hours advice line, groups for new carers, male carers, carers of teenagers and staying-put carers, a carer-to-carer mentoring scheme and paid membership of the Fostering Network. Applicants complete the three-day Skills to Foster course, and approved carers follow a personal development plan with training based on trauma-informed practice.
Before you decide, talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies below and compare what each offers.
